ranking_by: share of ordinary matter by mass
title: The 5 Most Common Elements in the Universe, Ranked (Gold Isn't Close)

scenes.text: Gold isn't on this list. Number one makes up almost three quarters of everything.

scenes.label: Neon · 0.13%
scenes.text: Number five: neon. Only about a tenth of one percent of the universe, the gas that glows in signs.

scenes.label: Carbon · 0.46%
scenes.text: Number four: carbon. Less than half a percent, yet every living thing on Earth is built on it.

scenes.label: Oxygen · 1%
scenes.text: Number three: oxygen. About one percent of the universe, forged inside massive stars.

scenes.label: Helium · 24%
scenes.text: Number two: helium. About twenty-four percent, most of it made in the first minutes after the Big Bang.

scenes.label: Hydrogen · 74%
scenes.text: Number one: hydrogen. About seventy-four percent. Nearly every star you see is mostly hydrogen.

description:
The five most abundant elements in the universe, ranked by share of ordinary matter by mass.
Hydrogen and helium make up about 98 percent of it. Everything else, including you, is the rest.
Which element surprised you most?
first_comment: Where would you rank gold? And what should we rank next?
